methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops targeting Hampton Roads signal grassroots capability-building outside traditional tech hubs, distributing foundational AI literacy through community-based learning rather than platform dependence or institutional concentration.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU-AI Ready RVA partnership creates institutional infrastructure for distributed AI education and community impact in Richmond, potentially seeding peer learning networks that could diffuse capability beyond the NoVA gravity well.

signals.title: Growth skyrockets for Virginia govcon startups
signals.signal_reading: Government contracting startup growth concentrated in NoVA reinforces the region's unique positioning at the intersection of federal procurement and venture capital, deepening technical sophistication but further concentrating AI-enabled business model innovation in the DC corridor.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches online workforce training program - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's online workforce training via ed2go platform signals shallow, credential-focused AI adoption in underserved regions—distribution without depth, creating platform-dependent users rather than autonomous builders.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: AI data center expansion critique highlights how infrastructure investment concentrates in NoVA's digital corridor while extracting resources (energy, water, land) from rural areas without distributing capability, crystallizing the urban-rural divide in Virginia's AI economy.
